issues.note: Also before the to-infinitive after wants is unnatural; Kim also wants to come.
Sentence-initial discourse use has different grammar; a separate sense is defensible.
Placement rules repeated across adaptation and synonym_discrimination; one fact, one field.
Also before be is attested in American English, but after be is the unmarked teaching norm.
Marked but grammatical; the error could be softened rather than removed.
Saying it is common in speech does not conflict with neutral labels; claim is broadly right.
Unnatural word order in a sense 1 example.
Note says before be, contradicting its own correction She is also a doctor.
Sentence-initial also is more typical of speech and informal writing; the explanation is accurate.
Fixed place contradicts sense 2 initial position and the usually in synonym_discrimination.
Correct: also wants to come is the natural order.
Also comes after be, as the correction and other notes show.
Plain short adverb-phrase definition is house style; not circular.
Learner-error note contradicts the after-be placement stated elsewhere.
Either rule stated in both synonym_discrimination and learner_errors.
Word-for-word repetition of the either rule across two fields.
Rightly identifies the wrong before-be statement as the conflicting version.
Similarly marks a parallel, not an added point; weak cross-reference.
Mid-position too is formal and rare; clause-end is the right teaching rule.
Example word order is unnatural for sense 1.
Similarly is not a synonym or real confusable of additive also.
Contradicts the correction and the other placement notes.
Similarly is a poor compare target; in addition or furthermore fit better.
Clause-final also occurs informally in American English; excessive-too point is irrelevant.
Unnatural; Kim also wants to come.
As well is indeed more frequent in British English; more common is not exclusive.
Too expensive is the degree sense, not additive too; irrelevant.

findings.F1: Sense 1 example 'Kim wants also to come.' has unnatural word order.
findings.F2: Learner-error note says also comes before be, contradicting its correction and the other placement notes.
findings.F3: Placement of also is stated in both synonym_discrimination and adaptation.grammar (one fact, two fields).
findings.F4: The either-in-negatives rule is repeated in synonym_discrimination and the learner-error note.
findings.F5: Adaptation note calls also's position fixed, contradicting sense 2's sentence-initial use and the 'usually' elsewhere.
findings.F6: similarly-adv is not a real synonym or confusable of sense 2 also.
